thread:
alex: heads up — last night we saw repeated shrink/expand cycles on the dedicated-gpu pool for europe-west that correlate with a single tenant's bursty jobs :eyes:
jean: ugh, saw that metric spike. did the allocator over-provision then immediately drain?
maria: looks like the admission layer allowed a 10x burst token grant, then the autoscaler reacted and removed nodes within ~2m, causing warmup thrash.
tim: can we reduce the token decay rate or add a smoothing window upstream of the scaler?
sophia: proposal: add a short-lived shared headroom bucket + telemetry-driven smoothing so we don't commit host churn for transient bursts. basically: admit into headroom first, only translate to node alloc after sustained pressure past window.
alex: that matches my thinking. rough DSL sketch I hacked this morning:

```
policy:
  smoothing_window: 90s
  headroom_bucket: 8p
  burst_decay: 0.3   # fraction of burst credit that decays per window
  persistent_threshold: 3  # #windows required to trigger node allocate
  fallback_profile: cpu-optimized-small
```

jean: love the DSL. couple of questions:
- how do we account for multi-tenant fairness if headroom is shared?
- how do we surface when a tenant is in headroom vs actually queued for nodes?
maria: answers:
- fairness: headroom is weighted by recent steady-state usage (so large payers get proportionally larger share) but enforce a hard cap per tenant to prevent runaway bursts.
- observability: add token_state metric labels: {mode=headroom|allocated|throttled} and a per-tenant headroom_usage gauge.

tim: ops concern — if headroom hides genuine capacity shortage, operators could be surprised. need an alert that fires when headroom utilization > 70% for >5m and node_count hasn't grown.
sophia: agree, add a telemetry rule and tie it to autoscaler dry-run traces so the oncall can see "would have scaled" decisions.
ops-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 1820001800 to test headroom admission with 5% traffic routing.
ale x: tiny nit: ensure fallback_profile triggers immediate low-latency model-variant for requests that cannot wait — degrade gracefully instead of failing.
maria: adding that. also we should run the sim harness with recorded traces from last 30 days to tune window and decay values before rollout.
jean: next steps: 1) implement admission headroom + metrics (maria), 2) add autoscaler dry-run traces + alert (tim), 3) run sim + propose tuned values (sophia). I'll own rollout plan and canary gating.
alex: sweet. thanks all. will follow up with a tiny PR for the DSL and a README for ops. :thumbsup:
